newsitem.title: USA: Edison 1,070 MW nuke seen on-line Mon night.
newsitem.headline: Edison 1,070 MW nuke seen on-line Mon night.

text.p: Southern California Edison Co hopes to have the 1,070 megawatt (MW) unit 2 at the San Onofre nuclear power plant back on-line around midnight on Monday, a company spokesman said Monday morning.
An estimate for how long the unit would take to reach 100 percent capacity was not immediately available.
The Nuclear Regulatory Commission reported early Monday that unit 2, which has been down for refueling and maintenance since November 30, had returned to "hot standby mode."
The unit's restart was delayed several times from an original early February target for unplanned repair work and was most recently scheduled to restart on Thursday.
But that schedule has been moved forward by a few days, the Edison spokesman said.
Meanwhile, San Onofre's 1,080 MW unit 3 is scheduled to shut for refueling on April 12.
The plant is majority owned and operated by Edison, while Enova Corp's San Diego Gas and Electric Co owns 20 percent and the cities of Anaheim and Riverside own the remaining five percent.
